subject: Annual planning orientation: OKR alignment & contingency ladders
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Sarah Kim <sarah.kim@acme-corp.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Annual planning orientation: OKR alignment & contingency ladders

Team —

Kicking off annual planning with a short orientation for leadership and stakeholders. Objective: align on high-level OKR targets, define the contingency ladders we will use across scenarios, and set the QBR readiness checklist and cadence.

Key asks in this note:
- Review the attached one-pager (annual_plan_prep_brief.pdf) with proposed timeline and decision gates.
- Confirm who owns each decision gate (go/no-go, budget tails, and escalation triggers) by EOD Wed.
- Bring any major risks that change target assumptions to the sync on Wednesday 3/24 (30 min).

Proposed timeline (compressed):
- 3/22: Orientation note + materials (this thread)
- 3/24: Leadership alignment sync (30m) — confirm primary targets and guardrails
- 3/29: Scenario ladders due (3 variants: base / downside / stretch)
- 4/05: QBR packet draft due

I attached a QBR_readiness_checklist.xlsx that maps deliverables to owners. Sarah — adding you since Acme is one of our reference customers; any changes on your side to timeline that we should consider?

Thanks,
Aditya
Aditya Rao
Director, GTM Strategy
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Sarah Kim <sarah.kim@acme-corp.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 10:01:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Annual planning orientation: OKR alignment & contingency ladders

On Mon, Mar 22, 2027 at 09:12 AM Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com> wrote:
> Team —
> 
> Kicking off annual planning with a short orientation for leadership and stakeholders. Objective: align on high-level OKR targets, define the contingency ladders we will use across scenarios, and set the QBR readiness checklist and cadence.

Thanks Aditya — quick notes:
- I can own the scenario ladders deliverable (3/29) but will need one SME from Product (TBD) and one from Revenue Ops to validate assumptions.
- Recommend we add a short budget sensitivity matrix to the spreadsheet (how much runway we buy by shifting hiring / marketing spend) so the finance partners can sign off earlier.
- If we aim to keep the 3/24 sync to 30m, we should circulate a 1-page slide ahead of time with the primary ask and the 2 decisions we need on that call. I can draft that if folks are OK.

I'll do a pass on the QBR checklist tonight and update the Drive link.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
VP, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 11:33:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Annual planning orientation: OKR alignment & contingency ladders

Thanks — a few operational constraints to flag before the 3/24 sync:
- Dedicated capacity sales forecasts are still being reconciled with infra supply; we should treat any high-throughput committed targets as provisional until supply reconciles in the 3/29 window.
- For the contingency ladders: define 3 levers (pricing elasticity, batch/caching aggressiveness, and hiring freeze) and show their approximate unit-economics impact. That makes trade-offs clearer for execs.
- Laura, please confirm whether Finance can commit to the shortened review cycle and the dates in the brief. If not, call it out now so we can adjust.

I'll join the 3/24 sync but may need to drop after 20m.

—Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Product & Ops
Redwood Inference
From: Sarah Kim <sarah.kim@acme-corp.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Hale <tom.hale@procurehq.com>
Date: Tue, 23 Mar 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Annual planning orientation: OKR alignment & contingency ladders

Appreciate the heads-up, Aditya — Acme is aligned with a similar timeline on our side. A couple of external notes:
- If you include an explicit SLA/latency assumption in the scenario ladders, call out the customer-impact buckets (Core, Degraded, Failover) so we can map to our procurement gating.
- Procurement (cc'd Tom) will want to see a short summary of any material changes to pricing elasticity you propose; that'll speed approvals.

We do not expect to change the 3/24 sync window. Looking forward to the 1-pager.

Best,
Sarah Kim
Director, Platform Strategy
Acme Corporation
